summary: This record contains the pair-level summaries, model-level matrices and analysis scripts for the manuscript Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Metric-Sensitive Reassessment . The archive covers 231 static pairs from 22 language models, a 153-pair multi-family static-to-contextual set from 18 models (Qwen 7, Gemma 4, SmolLM 4, Phi 3), and 91 layer-wise pairs from 14 models. The balanced set is analyzed with angular and Euclidean RDMs; the angular metric is primary. The archive includes the 22 x 22 Mantel, CKA, distance-correlation and Gromov-Wasserstein matrices, the 13 x 13 legacy proxy matrices, the 14 x 14 layer-wise Mantel and Procrustes matrices, the 153-pair extension table, the crossed random-effects inputs and outputs, and the scripts that reproduce them. Raw model weights, token-level distance matrices and cached hidden states are not included. The Procrustes values are shared-token subspace statistics, not full-width alignment. The static and multi-family sets are Qwen-heavy; the manuscript reports family-specific correlations and does not claim a uniform within-family effect. Code is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. Data and derived tables are released under CC BY 4.0. See README.md and PROVENANCE.md for file mapping, reproduction instructions and caveats.
title: Code and derived data for: Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Contextual Reassessment

summary: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

summary: This release contains 345 computed metamer mismatch bodies with their defining inputs and validation records. It also contains the software that computes and validates them. A metamer mismatch body describes how objects that match in color under one illuminant can differ in color under another. The collection covers six observer models and 38 illuminant pairs, each pairing D65 with a second illuminant. The wavelength spacings are 1, 2, 5 and 10 nm. The target colors are defined by flat reflectances from 10% to 90%. The manifest lists the combinations included. Each dataset contains five files. One is a generators file that defines the color mechanisms and the target color. The others hold the boundary vertices, the triangular faces, a summary and a validation certificate. The vertices and faces are CSV files. The method computes the exact body for the discretized problem. Coordinates are stored as floating-point numbers. Reflectances are bounded between 0 and 1 without additional smoothness constraints. The software includes MATLAB and CUDA sources, CIE input tables and a Slurm workflow for running the computations on an HPC cluster. Documentation covers configuration, a small worked example and recovery from interrupted jobs. Validation records describe file integrity, volume consistency and reflectance feasibility checks. The manifest and certificates report the validation coverage and numerical tolerances for each dataset. README.md describes each file and its license.
title: Exact Discrete Metamer Mismatch Bodies from Zonotope Tiling

summary: AUTONOMOUS MICROROBOTIC NAVIGATION FOR AGING MICROENVIRONMENT MAPS AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Institute XXVI | Flagship 01 What if a mobile microscale instrument could choose where to measure an aging-associated tissue environment, yet remain honest about the regions it cannot reach and the biological changes it might cause while observing? This prospective English research monograph develops an evidence-constrained framework connecting externally actuated microrobotic navigation, spatial phenotypes of cellular aging, and information-theoretic active learning. Its central hypothesis is deliberately falsifiable: under matched sampling budgets and strict disturbance limits, a pre-registered active route must reduce reconstruction error in independently withheld regions compared with optimized fixed-grid, passive-imaging, and random-navigation methods. Attractive trajectories, single-marker fluorescence, and confident maps are not accepted as substitutes for valid biological ground truth. The work is organized around a five-layer scientific architecture: three-dimensional phantom truth, traceable robot localization, safety-constrained acquisition, biological noninterference, and blinded cross-batch or cross-laboratory transfer. It includes 30 domain-qualified mathematical derivations, 82 research chapters, 410 separately paginated studies, 200 detailed Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence register makes explicit what external research supports and what remains untested. The accompanying Excel workbook connects Gates, equations, chapter pages, and evidence sources. The proposed studies are limited to engineered hydrogel phantoms and carefully bounded ex-vivo research. This book does not report newly conducted experiments, clinically approved autonomous nanorobots, human diagnosis, demonstrated rejuvenation, or lifespan extension. Its enduring aim is to leave future investigators a rigorous, revisable set of research questions, including the possibility that simpler instruments may prove scientifically superior. Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI White Rainbow Scientific Library | October 2026

summary: HHT is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, HHT aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://zhanchaoyang.com/HHT-app/docs/
title: HHT: An Open-Source, Privacy-First Travel Diary for Mobility Research

summary: This dataset provides monthly global ocean mixed layer depth (MLD) estimates at 1° spatial resolution from January 1982 to December 2023, developed using SJTU-ViT, a Vision Transformer-based reconstruction model. It contains 504 monthly fields on a regular latitude–longitude grid, with valid coverage defined by a fixed RECCAP2 open-ocean mask. The target MLD is defined by a potential density increase of 0.03 kg m⁻³ relative to 10 m. MLD estimates are expressed in metres, positive downward from the sea surface, with a lower bound of 10 m. Data are provided in NetCDF-4 format, accompanied by a README describing the variables, coordinates, MLD definition, masking, and data access.
title: A monthly 1° global ocean mixed layer depth dataset for 1982–2023 developed with SJTU-ViT

summary: Assembly traces can support explicit probabilistic inference without being treated as recovered program meaning. Active Assembly Theory and Practice makes that distinction executable: transparent x86-64 fixtures are decoded with Capstone, traced under bounded Unicorn emulation, and mapped to typed observations that distinguish missing, unseen, and unsupported evidence. Two Generalized Notation Notation (GNN) specifications define passive-phase and prospective sensor models whose tensors drive real pymdp execution. A native categorical Julia/RxInfer companion consumes the passive model's same parameters (Friedman 2026; Heins et al. 2022; Bagaev et al. 2023). The sensor Agent selects an action before fixture evidence is acquired. Independent finite calculations check beliefs and policy scores; native smoothing uses the same parameters and first-observation convention. Every inference comparator and fitted diagnostic also consumes an upstream-parsed numeric GNN specification, with source-bound runtime instances and rendered model graphs. A corpus of 10 authored fixtures supports complete-fixture exclusion diagnostics. At the fixed informative likelihood, the memoryless decoder outperforms the temporal filter; temporal advantages appear under synthetic observation ambiguity. Designed category ambiguity remains a visible failure case. The separate Gaussian and categorical Bethe free-energy diagnostics are not compared numerically with policy expected free energy. The quotient benchmark contains 64 transformation-family identifiers and 4096 rows, with 16 families held out from model fitting. The co-primary portfolio includes an interpretable classifier, a temporal probabilistic model, a fixed one-layer tanh recurrent classifier, and surface baselines; the temporal endpoint reaches balanced accuracy 0.775 and macro-F1 0.772 on this frozen bounded benchmark. Held-out identifiers share authored template lineages with the fitting data. Family-resampling intervals and conditional randomization diagnostics therefore describe this finite inventory; the retrospective protocol correction withholds superiority claims. A complementary pinned static-only corpus supplies 5 licensed source projects and 100 source-contract rows, including 40 lexical witnesses, 40 contract-directed near misses, and 20 identity controls. The corpus establishes provenance and coverage; it does not execute arbitrary external binaries or support application-effectiveness claims. Selected normalized machine-state relations are checked by Python, native execution, and a bounded Lean fragment. Exact finite sensing certificates and source-bound reader artifacts make assumptions and failures inspectable. Independent physical replication remains unearned. The contribution is a reproducible substrate for testing assembly-to-inference mechanisms, with explicit limits on semantics, statistical generalization, and external validity.
title: Active Assembly Theory and Practice

summary: Code, independent checks and the record of the Anaxia engine for the paper Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya. The paper determines, for the heterotic string with the standard embedding on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The 101 families are labelled by 101 distinct characters of the symmetry group (Z/5)^3, and the 24 characters that do not occur are the classes of the permutations of (0,1,2,3,4). Every Yukawa coupling allowed by the symmetry is a power of the modulus, psi^r with r = 0, 1, 2, 3 on 566, 425, 280 and 160 unordered triples, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that the mass matrix has determinant psi^70, full rank away from the Fermat point and rank 51 there, where the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. The Geometric Selection Conjecture is shown to be equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and no smooth quintic and no free quotient of one carries three families. On the three other one-parameter pencils of Fermat type, the sextic in P(1,1,1,1,2), the octic in P(1,1,1,1,4) and the dectic in P(1,1,1,2,5), the 103, 149 and 145 families carry only 96, 122 and 100 distinct characters of symmetry groups of order 108, 128 and 100; every coupling allowed by the symmetry is psi^r times a product of weights; the mass map of the invariant direction has rank 99, 125 and 109 at every member with psi nonzero, so 4, 24 and 36 families stay massless; and no member or free quotient carries three families. The existence of a viable vacuum is open. The archive holds 121 independent checks: a C program for the labels, the couplings allowed by the group and the mass map, a C++ expansion of the Hessian over its 120 permutations, Python checks of the socle, the Hessian, the intersection form of the Fermat quintic and the Gamma values, a Julia check of the Hodge norms, a Macaulay2 computation of the Jacobian ring at two rational values of the modulus with the socle functional on all 3876 monomials of degree fifteen, Python and Macaulay2 checks of the labels, characters, couplings, Jacobian rings and mass maps of the three weighted pencils, and 14 Lean 4 theorems on the counts, the arithmetic of the Hessian and the numbers of the weighted pencils, each axiom-free or depending on propext only. code/run_checks.sh runs them all. code/bllm/ holds the failure, change and retry record of the five targets on the Anaxia engine (release 3.1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23484160).
title: Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic: code, checks and engine record

summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode. Version 3.1.0 passes its mathematical-physics benchmark: every reflexive descent of each of the 473,800,776 reflexive 4-polytopes of the Kreuzer–Skarke list reaches a seed within 348 steps, so the Calabi–Yau seed conjecture holds; the sharp constants are 5 in dimension two and 11 in dimension three, and in dimension four the sharp constant lies between 22 and 348. The engine also learns from its failures: every failed attempt writes a record with its diagnosis and the one rule of the engine it changed, the loop is proved in Lean to stop, and a skill memory credits each change by the whole run it belonged to. The log holds 10 runs, 73 attempts and 57 rule changes, from the engine's own runs and from the attacks on simple zeros of the zeta function, the Erdős–Straus equation, union-closed families, lonely runners, the Dwork quintic, lattice Yang–Mills and points in convex position. On the Hodge conjecture, every convolution with at most seven line bundles on E 0 6 fails the polarised criterion at every discriminant, and so does every object supported on the 32 Weil threefolds. Of the six benchmarks only the seed conjecture is passed; the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdős problem 1183 stay open. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.
title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

summary: This reproducibility release accompanies the revised manuscript, Benchmark Integrity in Three COVID-19 and Mpox Misinformation Datasets: Duplicate Overlap, Cross-Dataset Contamination and Exploratory Label-Quality Signals . The archive provides Python implementations and analytical outputs for evaluating exact and near-duplicate content, evaluation-partition overlap, cross-corpus textual contamination, cross-dataset classification transfer, repeated-seed cross-validation and exploratory out-of-fold label-quality indicators across COVID-19-FNIR, Constraint and an mpox veracity-based analytic subset. Original third-party datasets are not redistributed. Data-source information and input-file checksums are provided to support independent verification.

summary: Where Yes and No Become Maybe The nested partner ring read as a folded square: a rolling stack, four providers, a straight-line gradient and a square-root address Driven by Dean A. Kulik  October 2026 Abstract The nested partner ring is Dean Kulik’s construction. Reverse a binary word, unless it is a palindrome, then complement it. Place the smaller member of every pair in ascending order on one half of a circle, set each partner directly opposite its word, and swap the two words that meet at the centre seam. The ring is never held. It is addressed. This paper holds the finished state first and reads everything back from it. Cut each word into its front half and its back half and plot it at the point whose coordinates are the front half and the reversed back half. Representatives fill the triangle above the diagonal of the unit square, partners fill its mirror image below, and palindromes sit on the diagonal, which is itself folded at its midpoint. The square is folded twice, and that double fold is the whole ring. Ten routes run back from the fold, and every one is an algorithm. The spreadsheet’s rolling columns are a two-provider stack, so the counter-clockwise column is the clockwise column three rounds later and the 8-bit cross pairs are the half turn. The ring is half built and half reflected, with a twist confined to its palindromic words. Every ring is the 2-bit ring used as a frame alphabet around the ring two lengths below: four providers, one of which is continuation, so continuation depth falls as 4^(-t) and averages 1/3. The representative density is the straight line 1-t, so a word of value t sits at angle t-t^2/2 plus a tent that is the fold of the diagonal. The seam is the apex where the density reaches zero. The complement branch compiles toward value 1/3 at angle 5/18. Rank and unrank need one quadratic, one integer square root and one bit-reversal count. The radial reader reads the digits of 1-√(1-2u) in the front half of every word. Merging each word with its partner leaves grey exactly where the two disagree: all of it at two bits, half of it in the limit, and all of it again on the diagonal and the anti-diagonal. Twenty-eight lines were sealed before their checks ran. Twenty-seven run as sealed. The twenty-eighth runs at every width except the degenerate width 1, where it lands elsewhere and is routed to its owner. Two claims from the previous session are withdrawn and routed. The open boundary is named in the ledger, Section 14. 1. The held state A word x of width L is an integer written most significant bit first. Write J for reversal and C for complement. The partner is P(x)={■(J(x),&J(x)≠x,@C(x),&J(x)=x.)┤ P is an involution with no fixed point: a palindrome is never its own complement and a non-palindrome is never its own reversal. This is the C1 axiom in its smallest form, since no word may hold its place without a partner to move to. The 2^L words fall into 2^(L-1) pairs. The representative of a pair is its smaller member. Representatives run in ascending order on positions 0 to M-1, with N=2^L and M=N/2. The partner of the representative at position i sits at N-1-i, and positions M-1 and M are swapped. The tape T_L is the ring read as L⋅2^L slices. The spreadsheet’s “sheet” reading, the circle read backwards with 0 and 1 swapped, is S_L=C(J(T_L )). At two bits the circle is T_2=00 10 01 11 and the sheet is S_2=00011011.   Figure 1. Rings 1 to 10, with radial thickness equal to word length and angle measured clockwise from the top. Left: light (1) and gaps (0). Right: every word merged with its facing partner, slice by slice, which leaves grey wherever the pair disagrees. The finished state is held before any route is walked. For even L=2n, split x=f∥g into a front half f and a back half g of n bits each, and place x at (φ,γ)=(f/2^n , J(g)/2^n ). The representatives are the cells strictly above the diagonal
title: Where Yes and No Become Maybe

summary: Where Yes and No Become Maybe The nested partner ring read as a folded square: a rolling stack, four providers, a straight-line gradient and a square-root address Driven by Dean A. Kulik  October 2026 Abstract The nested partner ring is Dean Kulik’s construction. Reverse a binary word, unless it is a palindrome, then complement it. Place the smaller member of every pair in ascending order on one half of a circle, set each partner directly opposite its word, and swap the two words that meet at the centre seam. The ring is never held. It is addressed. This paper holds the finished state first and reads everything back from it. Cut each word into its front half and its back half and plot it at the point whose coordinates are the front half and the reversed back half. Representatives fill the triangle above the diagonal of the unit square, partners fill its mirror image below, and palindromes sit on the diagonal, which is itself folded at its midpoint. The square is folded twice, and that double fold is the whole ring. Ten routes run back from the fold, and every one is an algorithm. The spreadsheet’s rolling columns are a two-provider stack, so the counter-clockwise column is the clockwise column three rounds later and the 8-bit cross pairs are the half turn. The ring is half built and half reflected, with a twist confined to its palindromic words. Every ring is the 2-bit ring used as a frame alphabet around the ring two lengths below: four providers, one of which is continuation, so continuation depth falls as 4^(-t) and averages 1/3. The representative density is the straight line 1-t, so a word of value t sits at angle t-t^2/2 plus a tent that is the fold of the diagonal. The seam is the apex where the density reaches zero. The complement branch compiles toward value 1/3 at angle 5/18. Rank and unrank need one quadratic, one integer square root and one bit-reversal count. The radial reader reads the digits of 1-√(1-2u) in the front half of every word. Merging each word with its partner leaves grey exactly where the two disagree: all of it at two bits, half of it in the limit, and all of it again on the diagonal and the anti-diagonal. Twenty-eight lines were sealed before their checks ran. Twenty-seven run as sealed. The twenty-eighth runs at every width except the degenerate width 1, where it lands elsewhere and is routed to its owner. Two claims from the previous session are withdrawn and routed. The open boundary is named in the ledger, Section 14. 1. The held state A word x of width L is an integer written most significant bit first. Write J for reversal and C for complement. The partner is P(x)={■(J(x),&J(x)≠x,@C(x),&J(x)=x.)┤ P is an involution with no fixed point: a palindrome is never its own complement and a non-palindrome is never its own reversal. This is the C1 axiom in its smallest form, since no word may hold its place without a partner to move to. The 2^L words fall into 2^(L-1) pairs. The representative of a pair is its smaller member. Representatives run in ascending order on positions 0 to M-1, with N=2^L and M=N/2. The partner of the representative at position i sits at N-1-i, and positions M-1 and M are swapped. The tape T_L is the ring read as L⋅2^L slices. The spreadsheet’s “sheet” reading, the circle read backwards with 0 and 1 swapped, is S_L=C(J(T_L )). At two bits the circle is T_2=00 10 01 11 and the sheet is S_2=00011011.   Figure 1. Rings 1 to 10, with radial thickness equal to word length and angle measured clockwise from the top. Left: light (1) and gaps (0). Right: every word merged with its facing partner, slice by slice, which leaves grey wherever the pair disagrees. The finished state is held before any route is walked. For even L=2n, split x=f∥g into a front half f and a back half g of n bits each, and place x at (φ,γ)=(f/2^n , J(g)/2^n ). The representatives are the cells strictly above the diagonal

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.

summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript submitted to Digital Discovery (RSC). The paper traces a cobalt-specific failure of conditional crystal generation back to one row of the public training data. Every number reported in the manuscript is recomputed from the files in this deposit by a single script (`verify_all_numbers.py`), which prints a mismatch count. This deposit is self-contained except for the training archive itself, which is 186 MB and is redistributed by its original authors; its exact provenance and checksum are recorded in `alex_mp_20_snapshot.json` so that the identical snapshot can be retrieved. Version v4 (revision). Adds the canonical generated structure files (5,121 chemical systems, 40,968 CIFs, assigned by reproducing the audit table system by system), the structures of the pre-registered generation tests, the generation command template and job files, the revision analyses (pre-registered tests A and B, equivalence test, upstream comparisons of the Co–O entries and hull vertices, DFT runs D1–D4) with the revision pre-registration, the figure-library modules and the recorded package versions. Element-level results are recomputed on the canonical set; the hull, DFT and intervention results of v1–v3 are unchanged. The verifier runs inside the deposit with relative paths and reports 0 mismatches.

summary: Abstract: A geometric construction of inverse-square gravity is presented in which solid angle accounts only for spatial dilution, while universal coupling to mass-energy supplies the physical strength of the interaction. This separation avoids treating a body-dependent geometric parameter as a substitute for gravitational mass. For a static spherical source, the construction recovers the exterior Newtonian potential per unit test mass, Φ(r) = -GM/r. Combining this static scalar potential with the special-relativistic energy of the escaping particle gives:   v_esc(r) = c * sqrt( 1 - 1 / (1 + GM / (r * c^2))^2 ) The result is subluminal for all finite r and reduces to the Newtonian escape velocity in the weak-field limit. The model is not presented as a replacement for general relativity, nor as a complete Lorentz-covariant field theory. Rather, it is a flat-spacetime scalar-potential construction that clarifies what follows from solid-angle dilution, universal mass coupling, and special-relativistic energy conservation before additional assumptions, such as wave propagation or optical-gravity extensions, are introduced.   Note on Versioning & Relationship to Prior Work: This paper presents a standalone, refined mathematical derivation focusing specifically on the static scalar formulation and relativistic escape condition. It serves as an independent baseline related to the foundational concepts outlined in the author's broader work ( A Solid-Angle Postulate as a Geometric Foundation for Gravity , DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19333670).

summary: RECONFIGURABLE ROBOTIC SWARMS AND CONTINUOUS FUNCTIONAL REGENERATION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Works | White Rainbow Scientific Library | Flagship 02 Prospective Research Atlas — English Review Edition, October 2026 Can a distributed population of heterogeneous modular robots reconstruct an operationally qualified capability after damage, without treating a newly assembled shape as evidence of restored function? Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit develops an interdisciplinary research program on modular morphology, distributed self-assembly, task-dependent graph structure, mechanical qualification, connector fatigue, recoverable actions, and independent post-reconfiguration verification. Its central proposition is deliberately testable: a swarm may change its topology after losing modules, but it earns the stronger name of functional regeneration only when its restored configuration satisfies the original, independently assessed service requirements and does not conceal emerging hazards or latent joint failures. The monograph distinguishes three often conflated networks: mechanical connections that transmit forces, communication links that transmit information, and power connections that transport energy. It then investigates how graph connectivity, geometric rigidity, elastic stiffness, buckling, frictional contact, thermal dissipation, material fatigue, sensing uncertainty, local negotiation, and safe rollback constrain what an apparently repaired swarm can actually do. A prospective twenty-module testbed provides recurring engineering anchors: bridge, gripping, and sensing-tower tasks, blinded removal of modules, unseen configurations, independent qualification, and strong comparisons with redundant fixed structures and specialist replacement procedures. The research architecture includes thirty mathematically diverse derivation plates, eighty-two chapter-level questions and their five individually paginated study units, two hundred falsifiable Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. The companion spreadsheet links physical models, chapter topics, prospective study cards, provenance, source DOI records, and page references to support future research and AI-assisted scientific handoff. Published robotics literature supplies a source-grounded context for modular reconfigurable mechanisms and fault-aware planning, including external DOI records for reviews and an existing fault-tolerant modular system. The manuscript separates those precedents from its own unexecuted research designs. Its two STARLI mother volumes are listed as conceptual ancestry, not as independent experimental validation. Biological regeneration functions as an analogy for staged assessment of restoration, not as evidence of biomedical efficacy, autonomous human-tissue repair, or indefinite machine life. This is a prospective research-atlas REVIEW EDITION. The mathematical relations, study proposals, design seeds, and acceptance thresholds are not experimentally validated findings. External mathematical review, whole-text DOI auditing, and a stronger editorial review for chapter-level semantic repetition remain necessary before scholarly publication. Negative findings, conventional method superiority, irreversible module retirement, and scientific abstention are legitimate outcomes within this research program. STARLI | 33 | White Rainbow Scientific Library

summary: 🌟 Summary Ultralytics 8.4.183 expands hardware deployment and improves reliability across training, prediction, data handling, and evaluation. 🚀 📊 Key Changes Axelera Metis support for every YOLO26 task: With Voyager SDK 1.9.0, detection, instance and semantic segmentation, depth estimation, pose, OBB, and classification models can all export, predict, and validate through yolo . The NMS-free detection path is used by default. SDK 1.8 exports remain compatible; the updated setup requires metis-dkms 1.7.0 or newer and supports PyTorch versions below 2.15. Higher Axelera throughput: In the documented COCO128 benchmark, SDK 1.9 reached 109 images per second at batch 32 , compared with 40 images per second on SDK 1.8. Larger prediction batches can improve throughput; batch size 1 remains useful when per-image latency matters. Intel acceleration for LiteRT models: LiteRT exports can now run on Intel CPUs and NPUs, including support for YOLO26 task types such as detection, segmentation, depth, pose, OBB, and classification. More reliable training and depth calibration: Fixes address warmup and gradient accumulation edge cases, MPS memory growth during training, and depth calibration replacing an already-good calibration with a worse one. Interrupted runs can also resume under the same Ultralytics Platform model, and W&B resuming works on Windows. More accurate and robust data workflows: Fixes improve ImageNet-subset classifier validation, accept UTF-8 labels with a byte-order mark, preserve non-ASCII grounding annotations, convert COCO RLE masks for segmentation, and align 16-bit NumPy images with image-file prediction behavior. Prediction, export, and visualization fixes: Negative FastSAM points now reliably exclude masks regardless of prompt order. Other fixes cover very thin images, rectangular INT8 calibration, grayscale LiteRT models, semantic overlay colors, depth-map saving, and several additional edge cases. Platform and documentation updates: Platform documentation now includes Gemma 4 and Nemotron as hosted annotation models and explains new visibility controls and workflows. Benchmark instructions were also clarified for NMS-free evaluation. 🎯 Purpose & Impact Deploy YOLO26 on more hardware and tasks: Axelera users can use one integrated workflow across all seven YOLO26 tasks, while Intel LiteRT users gain CPU and NPU inference options. Get better throughput when processing batches: Axelera SDK 1.9 can substantially increase prediction throughput for larger batches, though actual results depend on hardware and workload. Trust training, validation, and predictions more: The fixes reduce avoidable failures and make reported results better reflect the supplied data and model—for example, correcting classifier label alignment changes ImageNette validation accuracy from 9.45% to 70.37% in the reported test. Keep existing workflows working: Many changes are targeted bug fixes or compatibility improvements; notably, Axelera models exported with SDK 1.8 do not need to be re-exported for SDK 1.9. What's Changed Fix R/B channel swap of semantic mask overlays in train/val mosaics by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26755 Scale 16-bit NumPy prediction inputs to 8 bits by @Nikhi00718 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26741 Restore pre-existing temporary module aliases by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26756 Respect negative FastSAM points regardless of prompt order by @Nikhi00718 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26759 Align ImageNet subset folders with classifier class IDs by @Nikhi00718 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26760 Fix INT8 calibration crash when exporting with rect=True by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26750 Fix LiteRT layout detection for grayscale exports by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26747 Clamp warmup accumulate ramp to the capped

summary: 🌟 Summary Ultralytics 8.4.183 expands hardware deployment and improves reliability across training, prediction, data handling, and evaluation. 🚀 📊 Key Changes Axelera Metis support for every YOLO26 task: With Voyager SDK 1.9.0, detection, instance and semantic segmentation, depth estimation, pose, OBB, and classification models can all export, predict, and validate through yolo . The NMS-free detection path is used by default. SDK 1.8 exports remain compatible; the updated setup requires metis-dkms 1.7.0 or newer and supports PyTorch versions below 2.15. Higher Axelera throughput: In the documented COCO128 benchmark, SDK 1.9 reached 109 images per second at batch 32 , compared with 40 images per second on SDK 1.8. Larger prediction batches can improve throughput; batch size 1 remains useful when per-image latency matters. Intel acceleration for LiteRT models: LiteRT exports can now run on Intel CPUs and NPUs, including support for YOLO26 task types such as detection, segmentation, depth, pose, OBB, and classification. More reliable training and depth calibration: Fixes address warmup and gradient accumulation edge cases, MPS memory growth during training, and depth calibration replacing an already-good calibration with a worse one. Interrupted runs can also resume under the same Ultralytics Platform model, and W&B resuming works on Windows. More accurate and robust data workflows: Fixes improve ImageNet-subset classifier validation, accept UTF-8 labels with a byte-order mark, preserve non-ASCII grounding annotations, convert COCO RLE masks for segmentation, and align 16-bit NumPy images with image-file prediction behavior. Prediction, export, and visualization fixes: Negative FastSAM points now reliably exclude masks regardless of prompt order. Other fixes cover very thin images, rectangular INT8 calibration, grayscale LiteRT models, semantic overlay colors, depth-map saving, and several additional edge cases. Platform and documentation updates: Platform documentation now includes Gemma 4 and Nemotron as hosted annotation models and explains new visibility controls and workflows. Benchmark instructions were also clarified for NMS-free evaluation. 🎯 Purpose & Impact Deploy YOLO26 on more hardware and tasks: Axelera users can use one integrated workflow across all seven YOLO26 tasks, while Intel LiteRT users gain CPU and NPU inference options. Get better throughput when processing batches: Axelera SDK 1.9 can substantially increase prediction throughput for larger batches, though actual results depend on hardware and workload. Trust training, validation, and predictions more: The fixes reduce avoidable failures and make reported results better reflect the supplied data and model—for example, correcting classifier label alignment changes ImageNette validation accuracy from 9.45% to 70.37% in the reported test. Keep existing workflows working: Many changes are targeted bug fixes or compatibility improvements; notably, Axelera models exported with SDK 1.8 do not need to be re-exported for SDK 1.9. summary: Quantum illumination uses a retained idler to improve detection of a weak optical return in thermal noise. For a source designer, the practical resource question is how much ideal quantum storage is needed for a specified improvement. This work gives the exact asymptotic answer when the signal-photon budget and the total retained-register dimension are constrained independently. Exact finite-memory frontier Consider a thermal attenuator with transmissivity \(0<\eta<1\) and vacuum-output background occupation \(b>0\), tested against the replacer that returns the same thermal state. For \(n\) parallel uses, every admissible probe obeys a mean total signal-photon ceiling \(nN\) and a strict bound \(\dim R\le\lfloor e^{nP}\rfloor\) on the entire retained register, including retained source records. The memory rate is \(P/\ln2\) ideal qubits per use. With vanishing miss probability, the optimal false-alarm exponent is \[\Xi(N,P)=\eta\ln(1+1/b)N+G\!\left(\min\{P,g(N)\}\right).\] Here all logarithms are natural, \(g(x)=(x+1)\ln(x+1)-x\ln x\), with \(g(0)=0\), and \[G(p)=g(b)+p-F\!\left(g^{-1}(p)\right).\] The function \(F(x)\) is the entropy of the full complementary output for a thermal input of mean occupation \(x\); the complement includes the purification of the thermal environment. The first term in \(\Xi\) is the optimum without retained memory, and \(G\) is the additional detection benefit. The converse covers arbitrary normal mixed probes, correlations across channel uses and collective measurements. Matching sources satisfy the actual finite-register and energy bounds: they allocate photons between signal–idler correlations and a known displacement, and approach the frontier through finite-support preparations. How much storage is useful? The exact saturation rate and initial marginal value are \[P_{\mathrm{sat}}(N)=g(N),\qquad G'(0^+)=\frac{\eta}{1+b}.\] Because \(G\) is strictly increasing and strictly concave, at a positive signal budget \(N>0\) the minimum rate retaining a fixed fraction \(0<r<1\) of the full additive memory benefit is \[P_r(N)=G^{-1}\!\left(rG(g(N))\right)<r\,g(N).\] At low brightness, \(P_r(N)\sim r g(N)\). At high brightness, this fixed-fraction storage cost remains bounded while the exact-saturation cost diverges. The relative detection benefit simultaneously tends to zero: saving a large fraction of the saturation storage does not imply a large improvement over the total no-memory exponent. Connection to optical communication For the same thermal channel, let \(C(N,P)\) denote the classical capacity under the corresponding photon budget and a strict initial maximally entangled Schmidt-rank supply. The two separately defined tasks satisfy \[\Xi(N,P)-\Xi(N,0)=C(N,P)-C(N,0).\] This identity equates optimized incremental values, not the physical resources or protocols. The manuscript explicitly attributes the shared Gaussian-reference contraction and entropy-support tools to the capacity analysis. Its detection-specific contribution is the original-register mixed-probe converse, strict finite-register attainment and operational testing limit. Scope. The result concerns parallel, phase-known thermal attenuation, ideal retained storage and the vanishing-miss Stein criterion. It is an asymptotic resource benchmark rather than a finite-sample receiver or a noisy-memory optimum. The integrated article includes the complete proofs and two figure groups showing both storage cost and the value obtained from it.

summary: Precomputed results for DOST (Distance-preserving Optimization for Spatial Transcriptomics), a method for identifying spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data. This record accompanies the DOST code (see Related works) and the DOST paper. results.zip contains the outputs of the scripts in the reproducibility/ directory of the code repository, for DOST and for the baseline methods BANKSY, BASS, DR.SC, GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, stCluster and ADEPT. These are the files read by the figure scripts in reproducibility/figures/ . To use the files, unzip results.zip , set dir.output in the figure scripts to the unzipped folder, and run the scripts as described in reproducibility/figures/README.md in the code repository. The datasets are not included. They are publicly available from the BenchmarkST Zenodo records (DLPFC12, BC, mMAMP and mHypothalamus) and from 10x Genomics (Xenium Human Breast); see reproducibility/DOST/README.md in the code repository.
title: Precomputed results for DOST reproducibility

summary: TruLens 2.16 This release adds new evaluation metrics and Jury reliability metadata, improves handling of unparsable judge scores, and fixes cost accounting, batch evaluation, and OpenTelemetry tracing. Breaking changes and compatibility Streamlit-in-Snowflake dashboard support has been removed. ( #2784 ) All packages now require Python 3.10 or later. The test matrix now includes Python 3.14. ( #2896 ) New features Added a deterministic conversation_repetition metric. ( #2898 ) Added a requirement satisfaction metric. ( #2910 ) Added Jury.repeated and reliability metadata on every Jury result. ( #2854 ) Client hooks now adopt inherited W3C trace context. ( #2829 ) Fixes Evaluation scores and metrics Improved handling of unparsable judge responses: Excluded the parse-failure sentinel from score normalization, groundedness, and answerability scores. ( #2833 , #2834 , #2864 ) Dropped jurors whose judges returned no parsable score and excluded unparsable scores from per-item averages. ( #2837 , #2917 ) Excluded unparsable scores from BatchEvaluator aggregation, leaderboard averages, and compare_runs . ( #2866 , #2905 , #2939 ) Guardrails now reject unparsable and non-finite scores. ( #2902 ) Validated structured-output scores against the configured scale and corrected chain-of-thought context relevance scoring to use the requested scale. ( #2836 , #2860 ) Added response labeling to the agreement judge prompt. ( #2835 ) Added validation for retrieval relevance score lengths. ( #2853 ) Deduplicated ideal DCG by golden chunk text in ndcg_at_k . ( #2857 ) Skipped non-finite predictions during few-shot selection. ( #2852 ) Preserved min_score_val , max_score_val , and temperature in Metric.with_arguments . ( #2922 ) Fixed a pandas 3 get_group error when there is a single evaluation root. ( #2937 ) Corrected the llm_provider module import in jury.py . ( #2869 ) Batch evaluation and core behavior Read batch column mappings from the original row and preserved results when output column names collide. ( #2845 , #2844 ) Kept BatchEvaluator independent of the optional feedback package. ( #2901 ) Treated missing DataFrame cells as None and preserved columns in empty batch DataFrames. ( #2942 , #2946 ) Preserved retrieval order in context_filter results. ( #2932 ) Added a warning when TruSession is re-created with different settings. ( #2944 ) Cost accounting and reporting Prevented nested cost scopes from leaking callbacks into their parent scope. ( #2872 ) Fixed double-counting of evaluation spend in eval_cost . ( #2873 ) OpenAI cost tracking now adds per-call token and cost deltas rather than cumulative totals. ( #2855 ) Google provider cost accounting now includes thinking tokens and can price responses without constructing a client. ( #2861 ) LiteLLM cost tracking now accumulates across calls instead of retaining only the last call's cost. ( #2862 ) Anthropic now returns None for unknown model costs instead of reporting zero. ( #2856 ) Included child-span costs in OpenTelemetry leaderboard and trend calculations. ( #2912 ) Averaged per-input evaluation scores in the OpenTelemetry records view. ( #2909 ) Fixed handling of Postgres Decimal latency values in app metric trends. ( #2930 ) OpenTelemetry and client hooks Prevented generator span context from remaining active in the caller between chunks. ( #2914 ) Resolved default argument values when mapping instrument attributes. ( #2916 ) Client hooks now prioritize the traces-specific OTLP protocol setting. ( #2920 ) Added tracing for async methods wrapped in synchronous decorators. ( #2934 ) Prevented class methods from being re-wrapped for every new recorder. ( #2928 ) Provider and integration compatibility Bedrock now explicitly reports that response_format is not honored. ( #2795 ) LangChain now maps role="system" messages to SystemMessage rather than AIMessage . ( #2859 ) Added Claude 5 model support to the Anthropic provider. ( #2948 ) Documentation Documented UNPARSABLE_SCOR
title: truera/trulens: TruLens 2.16.0

summary: This record contains the pair-level summaries, model-level matrices and analysis scripts for the manuscript Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Metric-Sensitive Reassessment . The archive covers 231 static pairs from 22 language models, a 153-pair multi-family static-to-contextual set from 18 models (Qwen 7, Gemma 4, SmolLM 4, Phi 3), and 91 layer-wise pairs from 14 models. The balanced set is analyzed with angular and Euclidean RDMs; the angular metric is primary. The archive includes the 22 x 22 Mantel, CKA, distance-correlation and Gromov-Wasserstein matrices, the 13 x 13 legacy proxy matrices, the 14 x 14 layer-wise Mantel and Procrustes matrices, the 153-pair extension table, the crossed random-effects inputs and outputs, and the scripts that reproduce them. Raw model weights, token-level distance matrices and cached hidden states are not included. The Procrustes values are shared-token subspace statistics, not full-width alignment. The static and multi-family sets are Qwen-heavy; the manuscript reports family-specific correlations and does not claim a uniform within-family effect. Code is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. Data and derived tables are released under CC BY 4.0. See README.md and PROVENANCE.md for file mapping, reproduction instructions and caveats.
title: Code and derived data for: Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Contextual Reassessment

summary: Assembly traces can support explicit probabilistic inference without being treated as recovered program meaning. Active Assembly Theory and Practice makes that distinction executable: transparent x86-64 fixtures are decoded with Capstone, traced under bounded Unicorn emulation, and mapped to typed observations that distinguish missing, unseen, and unsupported evidence. Two Generalized Notation Notation (GNN) specifications define passive-phase and prospective sensor models whose tensors drive real pymdp execution. A native categorical Julia/RxInfer companion consumes the passive model's same parameters (Friedman 2026; Heins et al. 2022; Bagaev et al. 2023). The sensor Agent selects an action before fixture evidence is acquired. Independent finite calculations check beliefs and policy scores; native smoothing uses the same parameters and first-observation convention. Every inference comparator and fitted diagnostic also consumes an upstream-parsed numeric GNN specification, with source-bound runtime instances and rendered model graphs. A corpus of 10 authored fixtures supports complete-fixture exclusion diagnostics. At the fixed informative likelihood, the memoryless decoder outperforms the temporal filter; temporal advantages appear under synthetic observation ambiguity. Designed category ambiguity remains a visible failure case. The separate Gaussian and categorical Bethe free-energy diagnostics are not compared numerically with policy expected free energy. The quotient benchmark contains 64 transformation-family identifiers and 4096 rows, with 16 families held out from model fitting. The co-primary portfolio includes an interpretable classifier, a temporal probabilistic model, a fixed one-layer tanh recurrent classifier, and surface baselines; the temporal endpoint reaches balanced accuracy 0.775 and macro-F1 0.772 on this frozen bounded benchmark. Held-out identifiers share authored template lineages with the fitting data. Family-resampling intervals and conditional randomization diagnostics therefore describe this finite inventory; the retrospective protocol correction withholds superiority claims. A complementary pinned static-only corpus supplies 5 licensed source projects and 100 source-contract rows, including 40 lexical witnesses, 40 contract-directed near misses, and 20 identity controls. The corpus establishes provenance and coverage; it does not execute arbitrary external binaries or support application-effectiveness claims. Selected normalized machine-state relations are checked by Python, native execution, and a bounded Lean fragment. Exact finite sensing certificates and source-bound reader artifacts make assumptions and failures inspectable. Independent physical replication remains unearned. The contribution is a reproducible substrate for testing assembly-to-inference mechanisms, with explicit limits on semantics, statistical generalization, and external validity.
title: Active Assembly Theory and Practice

summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode. Version 3.1.0 passes its mathematical-physics benchmark: every reflexive descent of each of the 473,800,776 reflexive 4-polytopes of the Kreuzer–Skarke list reaches a seed within 348 steps, so the Calabi–Yau seed conjecture holds; the sharp constants are 5 in dimension two and 11 in dimension three, and in dimension four the sharp constant lies between 22 and 348. The engine also learns from its failures: every failed attempt writes a record with its diagnosis and the one rule of the engine it changed, the loop is proved in Lean to stop, and a skill memory credits each change by the whole run it belonged to. The log holds 10 runs, 73 attempts and 57 rule changes, from the engine's own runs and from the attacks on simple zeros of the zeta function, the Erdős–Straus equation, union-closed families, lonely runners, the Dwork quintic, lattice Yang–Mills and points in convex position. On the Hodge conjecture, every convolution with at most seven line bundles on E 0 6 fails the polarised criterion at every discriminant, and so does every object supported on the 32 Weil threefolds. Of the six benchmarks only the seed conjecture is passed; the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdős problem 1183 stay open. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.
title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

summary: This archive accompanies the article "A Reproducible Webots-Based Benchmarking Framework for UAV Mobility Modeling: Comparative Evaluation of Random Waypoint and Gauss-Markov Trajectories in Urban and Open-Terrain Environments" (Journal of Engineering, University of Baghdad). It contains everything needed to recompute every table and figure of the article from the recorded runs and to re-run any single simulation: - the Webots R2025a worlds (Open Terrain, and Urban with 50 buildings), with the building layout file; - the Python controller, which uses a cascaded PID flight controller with noisy GPS and gyro; - the Random Waypoint and Gauss–Markov reference generators; - the batch runner; - the analysis code (metrics, air-to-ground channel model, paired statistics with Holm correction) and its unit tests; - the 10 Hz logs and metadata of all 450 runs: 120 main runs (2 environments × 2 mobility models × 30 seeds), 210 runs of a memory-coefficient (α) sweep, and 120 ablation runs. A SHA-256 manifest lists every file. See README.md for the folder structure and for how to reproduce the results.
title: UAV mobility benchmark in Webots (Random Waypoint vs Gauss–Markov): code, worlds and logs of 450 simulation runs

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition — A Relational Physical Architecture from Quantum Possibility to Factualization, Retained History, Stabilization, and Spacetime

summary: Quantum illumination uses a retained idler to improve detection of a weak optical return in thermal noise. For a source designer, the practical resource question is how much ideal quantum storage is needed for a specified improvement. This work gives the exact asymptotic answer when the signal-photon budget and the total retained-register dimension are constrained independently. Exact finite-memory frontier Consider a thermal attenuator with transmissivity \(0<\eta<1\) and vacuum-output background occupation \(b>0\), tested against the replacer that returns the same thermal state. For \(n\) parallel uses, every admissible probe obeys a mean total signal-photon ceiling \(nN\) and a strict bound \(\dim R\le\lfloor e^{nP}\rfloor\) on the entire retained register, including retained source records. The memory rate is \(P/\ln2\) ideal qubits per use. With vanishing miss probability, the optimal false-alarm exponent is \[\Xi(N,P)=\eta\ln(1+1/b)N+G\!\left(\min\{P,g(N)\}\right).\] Here all logarithms are natural, \(g(x)=(x+1)\ln(x+1)-x\ln x\), with \(g(0)=0\), and \[G(p)=g(b)+p-F\!\left(g^{-1}(p)\right).\] The function \(F(x)\) is the entropy of the full complementary output for a thermal input of mean occupation \(x\); the complement includes the purification of the thermal environment. The first term in \(\Xi\) is the optimum without retained memory, and \(G\) is the additional detection benefit. The converse covers arbitrary normal mixed probes, correlations across channel uses and collective measurements. Matching sources satisfy the actual finite-register and energy bounds: they allocate photons between signal–idler correlations and a known displacement, and approach the frontier through finite-support preparations. How much storage is useful? The exact saturation rate and initial marginal value are \[P_{\mathrm{sat}}(N)=g(N),\qquad G'(0^+)=\frac{\eta}{1+b}.\] Because \(G\) is strictly increasing and strictly concave, at a positive signal budget \(N>0\) the minimum rate retaining a fixed fraction \(0<r<1\) of the full additive memory benefit is \[P_r(N)=G^{-1}\!\left(rG(g(N))\right)<r\,g(N).\] At low brightness, \(P_r(N)\sim r g(N)\). At high brightness, this fixed-fraction storage cost remains bounded while the exact-saturation cost diverges. The relative detection benefit simultaneously tends to zero: saving a large fraction of the saturation storage does not imply a large improvement over the total no-memory exponent. Connection to optical communication For the same thermal channel, let \(C(N,P)\) denote the classical capacity under the corresponding photon budget and a strict initial maximally entangled Schmidt-rank supply. The two separately defined tasks satisfy \[\Xi(N,P)-\Xi(N,0)=C(N,P)-C(N,0).\] This identity equates optimized incremental values, not the physical resources or protocols. The manuscript explicitly attributes the shared Gaussian-reference contraction and entropy-support tools to the capacity analysis. Its detection-specific contribution is the original-register mixed-probe converse, strict finite-register attainment and operational testing limit. Scope. The result concerns parallel, phase-known thermal attenuation, ideal retained storage and the vanishing-miss Stein criterion. It is an asymptotic resource benchmark rather than a finite-sample receiver or a noisy-memory optimum. The integrated article includes the complete proofs and two figure groups showing both storage cost and the value obtained from it.
title: The memory cost of quantum illumination

summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps. We introduce OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness organized around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory. The capability layer combines task-level tool interfaces with evidence rendering, providing consistent access to heterogeneous backends and converting their outputs into model-readable observations. Persistent multimodal memory retains the corresponding images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts throughout each query. A coding interface executes generated programs over stored data, enabling computations that combine results from multiple tools. Together, these mechanisms support an iterative process of acquiring, inspecting, and composing multimodal evidence. Evaluated on 22 benchmarks with eight open and proprietary backbones, OpenVLHarness improves average scores by 9.7-12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra. With GPT-6 Luna at medium reasoning effort, OpenVLHarness outperforms the base model, Codex, and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7-8.5 points while incurring at most 37% of their model-token cost.
title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory

summary: A seemingly reasonable push in Sokoban can make the puzzle unsolvable. To avoid such mistakes, an agent has to anticipate the consequences of its actions before execution, especially when feedback from the real environment is sparse or actions are irreversible. We introduce Agentic Imagination (Agima), a training framework that trains an agent to imagine before acting, i.e. to be imaginative. Agima trains a single omni model to propose actions, generate images of their outcomes, and then reason over these imagined futures to decide what to execute in the real environment. Rather than committing to a single plan, the agent can simulate a sequence of actions, explore alternatives, and compare possible futures. We first use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to unify policy and world modeling within a single omni model. This enables the agent to predict future outcomes and perform basic forms of imagination, such as forward thinking and counterfactual branching. We then use agentic reinforcement learning (RL) to teach the agent to reason with its imagined futures and use them effectively for planning. Across four environments spanning Maze2D, Sokoban, Pacman, and PushT, Agima generalizes to harder settings unseen during training. Trained with SFT alone on two-box Sokoban, Agima solves 40% of four-box puzzles while seeing the real board only once every five moves, compared with an action-only planner that only solves 2%. After RL, new behaviors emerge in how Agima uses its imagination: it learns a new unified format that was unseen during the SFT stage, learns to conduct forward thinking only when necessary, and branches more frequently at critical decision points. An agent that can picture where its actions lead can learn when and where to look ahead, that is, to plan. Project page: https://agima.net/.
title: Train An Imaginative Agent

summary: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model. For these uses to be reliable, however, the learned dynamics must behave well beyond the specific state-action combinations observed in expert rollouts. Despite this, the relationship between data coverage, dynamics generalization, and downstream planning performance remains underexplored. We study this relationship through the lens of compositional generalization: can a world model recombine familiar state and action factors into valid dynamics? To answer this, we introduce AnyGoal, a benchmark of goal-shifted task variants built from widely used world-model environments, together with an open-source library. Each task is designed to be within reach of a world model that has learned the underlying dynamics: individual state factors and actions remain within their training support, but their combinations are underrepresented in expert trajectories. Across multiple environments and world model families, we find that current models consistently exhibit failures under these recombinations. By examining dynamics and representation failures across model families, interaction regimes, and evaluation metrics, we study where current world models generalize and where challenges remain for goal-shifted prediction and planning. Together, this framework, benchmark, and analysis provide a basis for evaluating progress toward world models that generalize to new planning tasks.
title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts

summary: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.

summary: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.

We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.

summary: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. To this end, we introduce MemT-1.0, a new architecture of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation. Building on Metis, MemT-1.0 employs Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update mechanism within each turn. We further introduce Mixture-of-Storage to scale native memory capacity. Following a deliberate backbone preparation, we develop a two-stage training pipeline consisting of continued pre-training and post-training, supported by 34B tokens of training data and efficient training and inference infrastructure. We release a model family comprising MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation of memory and general capabilities. The results show that they outperform the parametric memory baselines on average and remain competitive with retrieval-augmented methods, while largely preserving general capabilities. At a history length of 128K tokens, MemT-1.0-Nano achieves approximately $1.86\times$ end-to-end inference speedup and a $66\times$ reduction in persistent storage relative to full context KV cache. By internalizing retrieved procedural experience, MemT-1.0 improves task success on agentic tasks, providing a practical step toward memory-native evolution.

summary: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.
title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
